title: What If Gravity Switched Off for Everything, Everywhere?
description:
What if gravity switched off, for everything, everywhere, all at once? Second by second, then hour by hour: why you wouldn't float up at first, why the ground would fall away from you anyway, where the air and the oceans would go, and what would happen to the Moon, the Earth and the Sun.

The premise is impossible. The speeds, distances and physics are real. 3D city scenes made in Blender with CC0 assets by Quaternius and Kenney.
core_message: Without gravity, Earth's spin would carry everything off its surface, and the planet and the Sun would come apart.
comment_question: What's the first thing you'd grab to hold on to?

scenes.narration: What if gravity switched off, for everything, everywhere, all at once?
scenes.heading: Gravity: off

scenes.narration: The strange part is what happens first. Almost nothing. Nobody shoots up into the sky.
Gravity doesn't push you up. It pulls you down. Switch it off, and you just stop being pulled.
scenes.heading: Nothing pulls you down

scenes.narration: Your feet stay on the ground, for now. Because something else is still going on. The Earth is spinning.
scenes.heading: But the Earth still spins

scenes.narration: At the equator, the ground under your feet is moving east at about four hundred and sixty five metres a second.
scenes.heading: Speed of the ground at the equator

scenes.narration: Gravity was what bent your path around the planet with it. Without it, you carry on in a straight line.
scenes.heading: You go straight. The ground curves.

scenes.narration: And the curved Earth starts falling away beneath you. Feet leave the pavement. Slowly.
After ten seconds at the equator, you're about one point seven metres up. Head height.
scenes.heading: Height after 10 seconds

scenes.narration: Where you live changes everything. At the poles the ground is barely moving, so people there simply float in place.
Minute one. Anything not bolted down is rising. Parked cars, bins, traffic cones, people.
By now, everything loose near the equator is around sixty metres up. As high as a twenty storey building.
scenes.heading: Height after 1 minute

scenes.narration: Buildings and trees are anchored, so they stay. Until they aren't. Roots and foundations were never built to be pulled from above.
scenes.heading: Only the anchored stay

scenes.narration: Meanwhile, the air itself is coming loose. Air pressure is just the weight of all the air above you.
scenes.heading: Air pressure is weight

scenes.narration: With no weight, nothing holds the atmosphere down. It starts expanding outward, into space.
scenes.heading: The atmosphere expands away

scenes.narration: As the pressure drops, water starts to boil. At low enough pressure, water boils at room temperature.
scenes.heading: Low pressure boils water

scenes.narration: Here's another twist. The Sun hasn't changed. Or rather, you can't see that it has.
scenes.heading: Watch the Sun

scenes.narration: Sunlight takes about eight minutes and twenty seconds to reach us. Whatever happens to the Sun, we see it eight minutes late.
scenes.heading: Light from the Sun to Earth

scenes.narration: And something is happening. The Sun only shines because its own gravity crushes its core hot enough for fusion.
scenes.heading: Gravity lights the Sun

scenes.narration: Without that squeeze, nothing holds the Sun together. Its hot gas starts flying apart.
scenes.heading: Nothing holds the Sun together

scenes.narration: Minute ten. The sea lets go. Water lifts off the surface in wobbling globes, while the city's loose ends drift above the roofs.
Ten minutes in, the people and cars that left the equator are about six kilometres up.
scenes.heading: Height after 10 minutes

scenes.narration: Up there, each breath holds less than half the oxygen it did on the ground, and the air is well below freezing.
scenes.heading: Thin, freezing air

scenes.narration: The same goes for Earth. Its core sits under pressure millions of times greater than the air at sea level.
scenes.heading: Earth is held together too

scenes.narration: About three hundred and sixty gigapascals at the centre. Gravity is the only thing keeping all that pressure in.
scenes.heading: Pressure at Earth's centre

scenes.narration: Take gravity away and the squeezed rock deep inside starts to spring back. The planet begins to come apart from within.
scenes.heading: Earth comes apart

scenes.narration: Hour one. Everything that left the equator is now around two hundred kilometres up. Higher than most weather ever reaches.
scenes.heading: Height in kilometres

scenes.narration: Hour two. More than eight hundred kilometres. Twice as high as the International Space Station.
scenes.subject: space

scenes.narration: The station has the same problem. Its orbit was just gravity bending its path. Now it flies off in a straight line too.
scenes.heading: Every orbit straightens out

scenes.narration: So does the Moon. It leaves on a straight path at about one kilometre a second.
scenes.heading: The Moon's speed

scenes.narration: Day one. Anything flung from the equator is about thirty four thousand kilometres up. Nearly as high as geostationary satellites.
scenes.heading: Height in kilometres

scenes.narration: The Moon is already about eighty eight thousand kilometres further from where it should be.
scenes.heading: The Moon, one day later

scenes.narration: And Earth itself, or what's left of it, stops circling the Sun. It carries on in a straight line at thirty kilometres a second.
scenes.heading: Earth leaves its orbit

scenes.narration: Year one. That straight line has carried the pieces of Earth past where Jupiter's orbit would be.
scenes.heading: Distance from the Sun, in Earth-Sun distances

scenes.narration: Every planet, every moon, every star, drifting in straight lines. Nothing ever pulls anything together again.
scenes.heading: Nothing comes together again

scenes.narration: Gravity is the weakest force in nature. And yet it's the one that holds your world together. So, what would you grab first?
scenes.heading: The weakest force holds it all
